headline: SoftBank is reported to be considering buying Allied Universal, the largest security services company in the United States, in talks that are still at an early stage.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a possible very large acquisition by a major AI investor, but the talks are preliminary.
importance_line: If a deal happens, guards, the public bodies that hire them (such as New York's subway operator) and SoftBank would be affected, but no decision has been made and the price is not agreed.
summary: Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that SoftBank Group is weighing a purchase of Allied Universal, which could be valued at up to 18 billion dollars in equity. Allied supplies guards to businesses, events and infrastructure, including New York City's subway, and has a large presence in security for data center building, but discussions are preliminary and no decision has been made.
notes: Same story as C11-04; the main session should keep one of the two. Bloomberg page blocked (robot check); text read from the Investing.com copy on Yahoo Finance, which credits Bloomberg. Reuters also carried it, citing Bloomberg News (Reuters page not readable here).
